subject: Tiered uptime slabs & proposed hot-patch window for Order Form redlines
messages:
From: John Carter <john.carter@vertexlabs.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: contracts@vertexlabs.com
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form redlines — uptime buckets and maintenance clarifications

Lukas,

Thanks for the draft order form. Our legal team attached a markup (Vertex_redlines_v1.docx) and had two specific asks I wanted to call out before formal redlines:

1) Service credit calculation: We'd prefer a stepped "slab" approach instead of a single percentage for any outage window. Example: 99.9-99.95 = 5% credit; 99.5-99.9 = 15%; <99.5 = 30%. Can Redwood map that to token/usage billing?

2) Emergency hot-patch window: We need a guaranteed 1-hour SLA for emergency patches during P1 incidents with an explicit carve-out for pre-announced security hot-patches. Our security team is comfortable with a small scheduled slot each month, but they want clarity on how it intersects with maintenance windows.

I attached the full redlines; happy to sync with you and legal for a 30m call today.

Best,
John
John Carter | Head of Procurement, Vertex Labs
john.carter@vertexlabs.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachment: Vertex_redlines_v1.docx (MS Word, 124KB)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>
To: John Carter <john.carter@vertexlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 10:33:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — uptime buckets and maintenance clarifications

John — thank you, got the doc and the examples. Looping in Marissa (account lead) and Kimberly (legal) to help finalize language. Quick responses inline below and then suggested next steps: 

- Slab/stepped credits: We can support a slabed credit matrix. I've attached a working spreadsheet (uptime-slab-matrix.xlsx) that maps uptime ranges to monthly credit percentages and the pro-rata token credit equivalent based on usage buckets. We should confirm whether the credits apply to invoice total or to specific affected routes — Marissa can advise.

- Emergency hot-patch window: We want to avoid an open-ended P1 patch SLA that forces immediate production restarts. Proposal: Redwood will provide a 1-hour response for triage and aim to schedule an emergency hot-patch within a 4-hour window where possible; full code-level remediation may take longer depending on impact. For pre-announced security hot-patches, we propose a monthly 2-hour maintenance slot where we will not count that time against availability.

Next steps: 
1) Kimberly/Legal to propose redline language for the hot-patch carve-out and the credit trigger definition.
2) Agree whether credits are applied at invoice level or per-route.
3) If both sides accept, we prepare an Order Form exhibit with the slab matrix and sign via DocuSign.

Can we run a 30-minute call at 11:00 PT to walk Vertex legal through the spreadsheet?

Thanks,
Lukas
Lukas Meyer | Account Executive, Redwood Inference
lukas.meyer@redwood.com | +1 (503) 555-0199

Attachment: uptime-slab-matrix.xlsx (Excel, 28KB)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas.meyer@redwood.com>, John Carter <john.carter@vertexlabs.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 Aug 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — uptime buckets and maintenance clarifications

Lukas/John — I've sketched proposed clause text below (high level) that legal can drop into the MSA/Order Form exhibit. Two points for commercial to confirm: whether credits are invoice-level or per-affected-route, and whether Vertex requires a maximum aggregate monthly credit cap.

Proposed (draft language):
"Availability and Service Credits. Redwood warrants Availability as defined in Exhibit A. Availability will be measured monthly. If Redwood fails to meet the Availability target for a given month, Customer will be eligible for Service Credits calculated in accordance with the Availability Slab Matrix in Exhibit A. Service Credits are the sole and exclusive remedy for availability reductions.

Emergency Hot-Patches. For P1 incidents requiring emergency code patches, Redwood will acknowledge the incident and begin triage within one (1) hour of Customer's P1 notification and use commercially reasonable efforts to schedule an emergency patch within four (4) hours. Pre-announced security hot-patches (notified at least 72 hours in advance) will be scheduled within Customer's monthly maintenance window and excluded from Availability calculations for the affected window."

Questions for the call:
- Do we agree to a single invoice-level credit by default, with the option to extend to per-route credits for larger deals (higher admin overhead)?
- If invoice-level, suggest cap at 50% of monthly fees per month (common guardrail).

I can be on the 11:00 PT call. If Vertex accepts draft text, I'll produce a tracked redline for the Order Form.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Attachment: none

Lukas — appreciate the quick turn. The draft slab matrix looks reasonable as a starting point; our legal asks that the spreadsheet be embedded as Exhibit A and the fallback remedy remain the credit matrix. Two quick requests before the call:

1) Can Redwood commit to the 1-hour triage + 4-hour patch scheduling for P1 incidents in the Order Form language (we need that in writing to proceed internally)?
2) We accept invoice-level credits conditional on a 50% monthly cap. Please prepare the tracked Order Form exhibit and a DocuSign link when you’re ready — our procurement team will need the full package to route for approval.

I'll be on the 11:00 PT call and will share the Vertex_redlines_v1.docx with inline comments shortly.

John
